customConcept.name: Robuchon au Dôme
customConcept.blurb: Seventy seats in the dome at the top of the Grand Lisboa, under a chandelier of 131,500 Swarovski crystals, with the largest wine list in Asia and three Michelin stars every year since 2009.

state.circumstances: You're the general manager of Robuchon au Dôme, at the top of SJM's Grand Lisboa in Macau. Joël Robuchon, the most-starred chef in the world, opened it; he died in 2018, and the kitchen keeps his repertoire alive under executive chef Julien Tongourian. SJM owns the hotel, the restaurant and a cellar of more than 17,000 labels; you run the room, the kitchen's budget and the three stars, and you answer to SJM's food and beverage leadership.

setting.name: The dome of the Grand Lisboa, Macau
setting.desc: The golden lotus-shaped tower at the heart of the Macau peninsula. Mainland collectors on weekend trips, high rollers sent up from the gaming floors, Hong Kong families marking an anniversary, and wine pilgrims who come for the list as much as the food.

ev.text: National Day Golden Week: the city is full, and so is the dome.
Grand Prix weekend: the street circuit brings the fans and the high rollers.
A typhoon signal 8 closed the ferries and the bridge for a day and a half.

log.text: You're the general manager of Robuchon au Dôme, at the top of SJM's Grand Lisboa in Macau. Joël Robuchon, the most-starred chef in the world, opened it; he died in 2018, and the kitchen keeps his repertoire alive under executive chef Julien Tongourian. SJM owns the hotel, the restaurant and a cellar of more than 17,000 labels; you run the room, the kitchen's budget and the three stars, and you answer to SJM's food and beverage leadership.

world.notes: Robuchon au Dôme is in the dome on the 43rd floor of SJM's Grand Lisboa hotel in Macau, under a chandelier of more than 131,500 Swarovski crystals. It has held three Michelin stars every year from 2009 to 2026, five stars from Forbes Travel Guide and three diamonds from the Black Pearl guide, and has won Wine Spectator's Grand Award every year since 2005 for a list of more than 17,000 labels, the largest in Asia. About 70 seats; lunch 12:00-2:30 and dinner 6:30-10:30, closed Tuesday and Wednesday; the August 2026 menus: at lunch, Menu Découverte MOP 998, Plaisir 1,398 and Gourmet 1,898, with a sommelier's selection of two, three or four 90ml glasses at MOP 588, 688 and 888; at dinner, the summer Menu de Saison (L'Été) at MOP 3,388 and the Menu Signature of Robuchon's emblematic dishes at MOP 3,888, both for the whole table only, and an à la carte from MOP 288 (cheese, desserts) to MOP 3,488 (Bresse chicken for two); all subject to a 10% service charge. Breads are baked in house. The wine-list items and the trophy bottles are real entries from the August 2026 list at its MOP prices. The wine list's foreword says wines are priced slightly above cost. The executive chef is Julien Tongourian; Joël Robuchon, who opened it, died in 2018. Most restaurants in Macau add a 10% service charge; restaurants have been exempt from Macau's 5% tourism tax since 2002; the pataca is pegged to the Hong Kong dollar at about 8.08 to the US dollar. The single tasting price here is the Menu de Saison at MOP 3,388 and its courses are that menu; lunch guests really pay less. The pairing price is the four-glass lunch selection, since the dinner pairing price isn't published. The menu, prices, hours and chef are from the restaurant's own published menus and page (August 2026); staff names below the executive chef, revenue, rent and the local events are estimates or invented.

profile.name: SJM Resorts
profile.kind: Macau casino and resort operator, the company Stanley Ho built
profile.desc: Owns and runs the Grand Lisboa and Grand Lisboa Palace; Robuchon au Dôme is the jewel of its restaurants.
profile.personality: Treats the restaurant as a flagship rather than a profit centre: the stars and the wine awards matter more than the margin, but the budget is watched.

rep.name: Vincent Leong
rep.title: Vice president, food and beverage
rep.style: Comes up for lunch once a month with a guest, asks about the Michelin inspectors before the numbers, and wants to know which high rollers dined last week.

events.text: A VIP gaming room booked the whole dome for a private dinner, and the cellar sold three bottles of 1982 Pétrus.
Mainland visitor numbers dipped after new travel rules, and the lunch sets went half empty for a month.

Macau.name: Macau

alcohol.note: Restaurants and bars serve alcohol under their Municipal Affairs Bureau licence; the casino hotels hold their own.

inspections.system: The Municipal Affairs Bureau (IAM) licenses restaurants and its food safety centre inspects them.

Macau.mealTimes: Lunch from about 12:30pm; dinner from 7pm, with the casino hotels busiest late into the night and on holiday weekends.
Macau.customs: Most restaurants add a 10% service charge, and tipping beyond it is rare. Much of the clientele is mainland Chinese, arriving for the weekend or a holiday; guests entertain, share and order big, and the wine list is a status symbol. UnionPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay are expected as well as cards.
Macau.labour: Labour law sets working hours, rest days and severance by years of service. Many hospitality staff are non-resident workers hired under government quotas, and resident workers must make up a set share.
